newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices seen positive in week.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices seen positive in week.

text.p: Factors underlying the strength in the wool market continue to be positive, pastoral group Wesfarmers said.
Sales this week are in Sydney and Melbourne with 72,000 bales rostered for sale.
"Although the extent of the recent price rises may limit gains this week, the strong underlying factors indicate the wool market will remain firm," Wesfarmers said.
The eastern market indicator rose 27 cents to 753 cents a kg clean last week, after touching a two-year high of 755 cents, while the western indicator rose 26 cents to 692 cents a kg.
This week's relatively small offering and a three week break during July is a major factor stimulating competition in the auction market, Wesfarmers said.

For overseas buyers, the effect of the rising wool price has been offset somewhat by the depreciation of the Australian dollar over the last month which has reduced the relative price of wool traded in other countries, it said.
Wesfarmers said demand for raw wool appears to be strong, evidenced by the flow of new orders and the large volume of wool purchased from the stockpile in recent weeks.
